subject: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Summary of needs: patient-facing summarization (short synopses), triage classification (3 labels), and PHI-safe redaction. Latency target is <= 200ms p95 for single-turn summarization.
- What we showed: hosted API + dedicated pinning option; example prompt templates for summary and classification; initial eval run against Acme’s 500-record test set.

Preliminary model recommendations based on the call:
1) rdl-3b-qa (quantized) — best balance of latency and factuality on shorter notes; recommended for classification and short summaries.
2) rdl-7b-v2 — higher factual accuracy on longer notes, slightly higher token cost.
3) rdl-7b-v1.3.2 — this is the stable release we used in the demo; we can pin to this version while we run a staged rollout of any newer model.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- You to confirm which priority workload you want as pilot (summary vs classification).
- We run a 1k-record eval on your side with our prompt set (attached) and our benchmark harness; we’ll share a short report within 48 hours.
- If you’re concerned about recent model updates, we can pin to rdl-7b-v1.3.2 for production traffic and test newer variants in a canary cluster.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.zip (prompt templates + seed examples)

I’ve cc’d Vivek to help with the benchmark run schedule — Vivek, can you propose two 1-hour slots this week?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0184
Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Rios <danielle@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — really helpful. We want to pilot the patient-facing summarization first (high priority). A couple follow-ups: 

1) We recently noticed a regression after Redwood pushed an internal model patch last month — our internal QA flagged more hallucinations on multi-paragraph notes. Before we commit to any rollout we need clarity on: what changed in the newer model weights/optimizers and whether there’s a straightforward rollback/pinning option.

2) Can you share the benchmark dashboard and the seed prompts you used in the demo? We’d like to run the same prompts against our in-house golden set.

3) Procurement will want an initial scope of work and an estimate for a 3-month pilot on Dedicated.

Attn procurement: can someone from your side confirm availability for a terms/price call?

Best,
Danielle Rios
Lead PM, Clinical Experience | Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Danielle — quick responses inline and a proposed plan: 

1) Regression context: the update you’re referencing is likely the v1.4.0 rollout that included a specialized instruction-tuning pass and a newer tokenizer config to reduce tokenization drift on long clinical notes. In some cases we observed small shifts in generation patterns for multi-paragraph inputs (the team flagged these in internal evals). We own that and have a couple of mitigations:
   - Immediate option: pin production traffic to rdl-7b-v1.3.2 (the stable prior release). Pinning is trivial and reversible — we can do this at the tenant level for Dedicated or via a tenant routing rule for Hosted.
   - Short-term: rollout v1.4.0 to a canary with your test set and check diffs in our evaluation harness.
   - Long-term: if you prefer, we can run a fine-tune/adapter pass on top of v1.4.0 with your in-domain examples.

2) Benchmark & prompts: attached is the prompt pack we used (acme_prompt_set_v1.zip) and I’ve uploaded the harness summary: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/acme/benchmarks/20260310-summary.html. That dashboard shows token-level latency, BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics we used for your summaries, and per-seed diffs between v1.3.2 and v1.4.0.

3) Procurement scoping: Rafael, can you draft a 3-month pilot estimate and a simple SOW? Danielle, procurement: if you share your internal constraints (SLA, data residency, support windows) we’ll include them.

Proposed immediate plan (mutual action plan):
- Today/Tomorrow: Rafael runs a focused eval (1k records) of v1.3.2 vs v1.4.0 using your golden set and our prompt pack.
- 48 hours: we provide a diff report + recommended pin/rollback decision.
- Week 1: if pinning required, we pin to v1.3.2 in production and run a canary of v1.4.0 on a subset.

If that sounds good, Rafael will kick off the eval — Rafael, please confirm ETA.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Danielle / team —

I started the eval job this morning (run id: RUN-ACME-20260310-01). Details:
- Dataset: Acme golden set (500 records initially, will scale to 1k if results look unstable).
- Models compared: rdl-7b-v1.3.2 (baseline) vs rdl-7b-v1.4.0 (candidate).
- Metrics: summary ROUGE-L / factuality heuristics (entity retention), hallucination count, token-level latency.

Preliminary note: on a quick spot-check a few long-case notes show more appended speculative text on v1.4.0; we’ll quantify in the diff report.

I’m attaching: acme_benchmark_summary_20260310.pdf (preliminary diffs) and the prompt pack (again) so procurement/devops can reproduce.

Pinning & rollback approach:
- For Dedicated: we can pin tenant -> model_version at the control plane; rollback is a single API call and propagates within ~5 minutes to serving nodes.
- For Hosted: we can set a routing policy to route Acme’s API keys to v1.3.2 and leave default traffic on v1.4.0.

ETA: full 1k run + formal report by 2026-03-11 09:00 PT.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: acme_benchmark_summary_20260310.pdf; acme_prompt_set_v1.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rios <danielle@acmehealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Danielle — attaching Rafael’s report and the prompt pack again for your team. High-level recommendation from Rafael’s run: pin to rdl-7b-v1.3.2 for the initial production pilot. The diff report highlights areas where v1.4.0 produces extra speculative sentences on long notes (see section 2.3 in the PDF).

Next logistics items: 
- If procurement signs the SOW, we’ll schedule a Dedicated capacity reservation (3-month pilot) and pin the tenant to v1.3.2 on day 1.
- If you want us to test a custom fine-tune, we can scope a small adapter job — Rafael, please add cost/turnaround to the SOW.

Danielle, are you available for a 30-minute sync Thursday to review the report with Rafael and Vivek? I’ll send a scheduling invite once you confirm a time window.

Thanks everyone — we’ll keep this lightweight and reversible so Acme can get reliable results quickly.

Best,
Marissa
